short: Faster abilities bring your next turn sooner.
long: Turn order is a clock, not a queue: after acting, a unit's next turn arrives in Initiative-cost x 100 / EFFECTIVE Speed ticks - effective, so every speed change really does bend it. Every ability lists its Initiative cost (a basic action costs 2.0) - a cheap, quick ability means you act again sooner, a heavy one leaves you exposed longer. Slowed cuts speed a quarter; Chilled cuts it a quarter at one stack and a half at two or more, so a chilled enemy genuinely waits longer between turns; Quick Draw shrinks the wait. The opening roll of the battle reads effective speed too, so a fight that starts with everyone Chilled or Frenzied starts in the order that implies. Losing a turn to Stun, Freeze, or Break still pushes the clock forward a full basic action - but a Cryomancer's Glacial Hold is not a lost turn, it is removal: a held enemy leaves the bar entirely until he releases it - except a held boss, which loses its turn like any frozen unit and shrugs the ice off after {=Battle.ORDINARY_FREEZE_TURNS} turn. The bar across the top of the battle shows the coming turns; hovering an ability shows a gold ghost of where it would put your next one.

short: A second turn taken immediately, and your own statuses tick again for it.
long: An extra turn is a WHOLE turn, not a free action. When one is granted you are pulled straight to the front of the initiative bar and act again at once - and because it is a real turn, everything that happens at the start of YOUR turn happens again: your damage-over-time effects bite, your buffs and shields count down, and your cooldowns tick. That last part is usually in your favour. What does NOT re-tick is anything standing on an ENEMY: their Burn, Poison and Chill count down on THEIR turns, so the board you spent a turn arming is untouched by your second action. Preparation (Survivalist) grants one, and it is deliberately DELAYED - you take the extra turn after your NEXT turn, not this one, so it is a setup card rather than a way to act twice on the spot, and it cannot be cast while its turn is still waiting. Two Warrior runes grant one on the spot: Last Word when he is brought below a quarter health, and the Berserker's Slaughterhouse when an enemy bleeds out. One nearby effect is NOT an extra turn and is worth telling apart: Rally hands one other HERO the next slot in the order (they still spend that turn, and nobody gains one).

short: Stop the sweeping marker in the center — for a stronger action, and on defensive heroes for a softer blow. Pure buffs and basic attacks run no check; the Sharpshooter's basic runs a multi-press sequence.
long: Most actions you take run a timing check: a marker sweeps the bar (about 1.0s each way) - press SPACE or click to stop it. NOT EVERY ACTION RUNS ONE. An ability with no damage and no Break damage - a pure buff, a shield, a pure debuff applier - has nothing for the grade to multiply, so it resolves at a fixed Good with no bar and its old Perfect bonus folded into what it always does. Healing abilities DO keep their check, because a heal's magnitude is multiplied by the grade, and so does anything that carries Break damage even with no HP damage. Basic attacks resolve at a fixed Good as well - except the Sharpshooter's, which still runs its check and runs it as a SEQUENCE (below). The gold center is PERFECT: +15% damage or healing, +25% Break damage, and many abilities add a unique bonus effect on top. The green band is Good: full normal effect. Outside both is Sloppy: only {=Ability.GRADE_DMG_MULT.fail*100}% damage and half the Break damage. The check never changes your chance to miss or be parried, and only three Perfects touch a crit - Execute's, Sweeping Strikes' and Triple Shot's; otherwise it multiplies what lands. Your timing matters as much as your build. THREE SPECIAL CASES USE THE SAME BAR. GATED ABILITIES: five abilities do not resolve AT ALL on a Sloppy - Death Ray, Requiem, Reckless Abandon, Boil Over and Unleash. Good and Perfect both resolve normally, so the gate is Sloppy alone. A gated failure costs the turn and nothing else: the resource is unspent, the cooldown never starts, and the meters those abilities consume are untouched - the enemy keeps its Ruin, the companion keeps its Loyalty, the Berserker keeps his whole Rage bar. Each of the five says so on its button, in its tooltip, on its draft card and on the bar itself, so the stakes are known before the cast is committed. No revival is ever gated, and no card whose purpose is healing: Requiem heals every hero as it consumes Ruin, but it is a damage card, gated like the other four. THE DEFENSIVE CHECK: the Warden always, and the Swordmaster while in the Defensive guard (Formless counts as both guards), run a check on INCOMING attacks too - once per attack rather than per strike, and with no Cancel button, because a hero cannot decline to be attacked. A Perfect brace cuts that attack's damage by 15% and its Break damage by 25%. Good and Sloppy are identical there and never worse, so a defensive check can only ever help. THE SHARPSHOOTER'S SEQUENCE: his BASIC ATTACK ONLY - no other ability of his - runs one press plus one more for every {=Battle.SS_SEQ_STEP} Focus he is holding when the bar opens, capped at FOUR. The cap is deliberate: Focus has no ceiling, and an uncapped rule would turn deep Focus into a sequence nobody can physically press. Every landed press counts and a miss ENDS the sequence while keeping everything earned before it, so a four-press attempt that misses on the second is worth one press rather than nothing; landed means Good or better. It pays in FOCUS, not damage: {=Battle.SS_SEQ_FOCUS_PER_PRESS} Focus a landed press, and a further {=Battle.SS_SEQ_FULL_BONUS} for a full sequence. Damage resolves off the FIRST press's grade exactly as an ordinary basic does - the later presses add none - so deep Focus makes him ramp faster rather than hit harder per swing. Each press is narrower than the one before it, and the opening window widens as the press count rises, so landing the whole sequence is about as achievable at 150 Focus as at 0. His bar is the one spec that is meant to be harder than everyone else's, by a flat 15% less timing tolerance at every press count, and it sweeps faster to match.

short: Attacks fill a Break meter; a full meter costs the victim a turn.
long: Alongside HP damage, most attacks carry Pressure - Break damage (BD) - which fills the target's Break meter (0-100). High Constitution shrinks incoming BD proportionally; crits deal 1.5x BD. The meter never drains on its own: it keeps climbing until it fills and the unit BREAKS - losing its next turn, dropping 30% of its armor, and taking +25% crit chance against it. When the Broken turn passes, the unit recovers and its meter empties back to zero. Breaking a boss also strips its immunity to stuns and mind magic for the duration.

short: {=Battle.CRIT_CHANCE*100}% base chance: 1.5x damage and 1.5x Break damage. Chance past 100% becomes multiplier.
long: Attacks have a {=Battle.CRIT_CHANCE*100}% base chance to crit for 1.5x damage and 1.5x Break damage. A Broken target takes +25% crit chance from everyone. Many talents and spec mechanics push the roll further - the Sharpshooter's Focus adds +{=Unit.FOCUS_STEP*100}% per point up to its conversion point (past which it buys critical MULTIPLIER instead) and every attack he lands without a critical adds +{=Unit.PITY_CRIT_STEP*100}% more until his next one, Resonance stacks add a flat +1% each for the Arcanist, and Aguila's bond shares +10% with every hero. Only a few effects raise the 1.5x multiplier itself. AND CHANCE PAST A CERTAINTY IS NOT WASTED: a total above 100% cannot make a hit more certain, so every point of surplus is paid as critical damage instead, +{=Battle.CRIT_EXCESS_STEP} of multiplier for 1.0 of surplus chance. It is the assembled total that converts and not any single source, so it is a deep-build reward rather than any one talent's - and it is separate from the Sharpshooter's own conversion, which reads a depth in one meter. Both can pay on the same blow.

short: A multi-hit ability spends one charge and fires its on-hit effects PER STRIKE.
long: Some abilities strike more than once from a single cast - three shots into one enemy, a volley, a flurry. WHEN ONE OF THOSE MEETS A CHARGE BANK OR AN ON-HIT EFFECT, EVERY STRIKE COUNTS SEPARATELY. Arcane Arrows banks six charges and each of the next six HITS forks into a second enemy - so a three-shot Aimed Volley spends THREE of the six and forks three times, not one and once. The same rule runs the other way: Mirror Image's images are spent one per incoming hit, so a three-strike blow eats three of them. A strike that MISSED or was BLOCKED spends nothing - a charge rides a blow that landed. This is a real power increase for multi-hit abilities and it is deliberate: it is what makes a multi-hit kit and a charge bank a BUILD rather than a coincidence. Area attacks are the exception that proves it - they roll no miss at all, so they never spend an image.

short: The damage an ability deals as its blow lands.
long: A strike is the damage an ability deals as its blow lands. A status's tick, a detonation, a bleedout burst, a reflection and a bomb are not strikes, and a bonus to strike damage does not reach them. Nor does such a bonus, or a ward against strikes, reach a strike a card deals by a rule of its own, as a Killing Frost does; and a ward does not lessen a companion's blow.

term: The Enemy With the Most Health
short: Where a rule picks an enemy for you, it is the one with the most health left - the first in the warband on a tie.
long: Some rules choose the enemy themselves: the Blood Debt rune bills the enemy with the most health for Blood Price, and the Tracker's and the Arbiter's marks, when the enemy wearing one falls, move to the enemy with the most health. It is the living enemy with the most health LEFT, counted in points rather than as a share - so a large enemy at half health is picked over a small one untouched. On a tie it is the first in the warband, the order the enemies stand in. No die is rolled, so the pick can be planned around.

short: {=Battle.MISS_CHANCE*100}% base chance for most single-target attacks to whiff.
long: Single-target attacks miss {=Battle.MISS_CHANCE*100}% of the time at base - all but a counter and the few strikes an ability deals by its own rule (Shield Slam, Feint, Precision Strike), which never roll one. Being Dazed adds +20%, Blind adds +50%, and attacking an Elusive target adds +25%. Area attacks never miss. A miss deals nothing at all - no damage, no Break, no on-hit effects.

short: A parried hit still lands, but at a quarter strength.
long: Heroes parry incoming melee attacks {=Unit.HERO_PARRY_CHANCE*100}% of the time at base, the Swordmaster {=Classes.SPEC_INFO.swordmaster.parry_chance*100}% (enemies {=Battle.ENEMY_PARRY_CHANCE*100}%); talents and buffs raise it; no stance does. A parried hit is not negated - it lands at 25% damage and 25% Break damage. Ranged attacks cannot be parried unless the defender holds the Deflection talent, area attacks cannot be parried, and a Broken unit cannot parry at all.

short: The Swordmaster fights Aggressive or Defensive; four abilities switch him, and three REQUIRE a guard.
long: The stances are the Swordmaster's: only his Seasoned Fighter pays their terms, though a drafted guard card reads and flips any Warrior's. He is normally in one of two - FORMLESS is the one card that puts him in neither and both at once. AGGRESSIVE: +{=Unit.SEASONED_AGG_DEALT*100}% damage dealt and +10% damage taken. DEFENSIVE: 15% less damage taken and -10% damage dealt. He starts every battle Aggressive, and the stance resets with each new battle - it is never carried between fights. FOUR abilities change it: Guard Change, which pivots, presses the opening and builds Rage; and three drafted cards, Precision Strike, Feint and Wheeling Cut, which BRANCH on the stance they are cast from and then switch it. A parry under Battle Poise buys him a free pivot as well. The drafted cards branch the same way round, and it is worth knowing: each branch buys what the stance he is ARRIVING in wants. Cast from Aggressive he lands in Defensive, so he is handed defence - a parry buff, or an enemy whose next attack lands on its own side. Cast from Defensive he lands in Aggressive, so he is handed offence - an armor bypass, or charges that parry blows and return them. He is never stranded mid-pivot.

short: Some Swordmaster cards can only be cast from one guard - the button stays dark in the other.
long: A stance-gated ability REQUIRES a guard rather than behaving differently in each one. Sever can only be cast from the Aggressive stance and Battle Poise only from the Defensive; in the wrong guard the button is simply unavailable, not weaker. Casting one does NOT switch his stance - that is the difference from a stance READER. Precision Strike and Feint are readers: they work in either guard, do something different in each, and then flip him. FORMLESS is the widest answer to being locked out: while it holds he counts as BOTH guards, so every gated card in his kit is castable - and he cannot Guard Change, because there is no stance to change. Feigned Guard is the cheaper, narrower answer: for 3 turns his abilities resolve as though cast from the OTHER guard and satisfy that guard's requirement, while he keeps the stance he is actually standing in - so an Aggressive Swordmaster can cast Battle Poise without giving up Aggressive's damage. Guard Change is still the free, unconditional way to move between the two.

short: The dead sit the fight out - but victory brings everyone back.
long: A hero at 0 HP falls: they lose every status and take no turns until raised, though a Burn or Poison they laid goes on burning. Mid-battle, a Revive Potion brings them back at 50% HP and the Cleric's Resurrection at 25% (at full health when Empowered). If the heroes WIN the battle, the Untouched refuse to stay down: every hero - fallen or merely battered - leaves the fight with at least 20% of their max HP. Only losing everyone ends the run.

short: A HERO is one of your four. An ALLY is a hero OR a companion - and the two words are not interchangeable.
long: Your side of the field can hold more than four bodies. The four are HEROES. A Hunter's companion - Ursus, Canis or Aguila, called by Summon Companion, which every Hunter but the Sharpshooter carries - fights beside them, takes hits, and can be healed, but it is NOT a hero: it is an ALLY, and so is every hero. The distinction is load-bearing because most broad talents deliberately pay the four and not the companion, so the wording tells you which you are getting. An effect that says HERO pays the four - Bulwark of Fortitude, the Occultist's Ruin heals, War Stomp and Rallying Shout's RESOURCE clause (each pays the OTHER heroes and not the caster, and a companion has no resource bar to fill), and the talents We Do Not Break and Heal More When Low (both stamped on the four before any companion is called). So do four more: Consecrated Ground (its mitigation is a choice, but its Faith drip is refused twice over - a companion takes no turn and Faith itself is heroes-only), Divine Wrath (BOTH halves fail, and for different reasons - the damage is read in a strike loop a companion's blows never enter, the speed in a turn order it is not in), Battle Shout's damage (the same strike loop) and Sacred Resolve (its apply and all three of its splits walk the four). An effect that says ALLY pays companions too - Hold the Line's Break cut and its no-death window, Sanctuary's heal, the cleanses of the talent Cleanse Debuffs Each Turn, Harvest's reading of who opened a wound, and Rallying Shout's Pressure clause (a companion has a Break meter, so it sheds the 30 like anyone else). Targeting follows the same rule: a single-target support ability you aim by hand CAN be aimed at a companion (Rally excepted: it hands its slot to a HERO), so Divine Shield on the bear is a legal and sometimes correct play. Faith is heroes-only outright - a companion can never hold a stack of it. RALLYING SHOUT IS THE WORKED EXAMPLE OF A CARD WITH TWO CLAUSES OF DIFFERENT SHAPE: its Pressure half says ALLY and reaches a companion's Break meter, and its resource half says HERO in the same sentence, because a companion has no resource bar. AND A CLAUSE CAN BE NARROWER THAN EITHER WORD: Battle Shout and Hold the Line each hand FIVE RAGE TO THE CASTER ALONE, which is neither the four nor the five, so each card says so in its own sentence rather than inside the group clause.

short: Loses next turn. -30% armor, +25% crit chance against this unit.
long: The Break meter filled: this unit loses its next turn, its armor drops by 30%, everyone crits it +25% more often, and it can neither Block nor parry. A Broken boss also loses its immunity to stuns and mind magic. When the lost turn passes the unit recovers and its Break meter resets to zero - the window is short, so spend it hard.

short: Loses their next turn.
long: A stunned unit skips its next turn entirely (statuses and cooldowns still tick during the skipped turn). Bosses are immune unless Broken - except to a Perfect Pommel Strike. Sources include Pommel Strike and sprung traps.

short: -25% speed; turns arrive later.
long: Slowed cuts speed by 25%, which pushes every turn booked while it holds later on the initiative timeline - the turn already waiting when it lands keeps its place. It does not stack with itself - reapplying just refreshes the longer duration.

short: Stacking frost: slower at one stack and slower again at two; 4 stacks freeze solid.
long: Chill stacks up to 4: one stack is -25% speed, two is -50%, three also cuts the victim's damage dealt by 15%, and the fourth FREEZES them. A new application resets the timer of the whole pile. Chill applied by a Cryomancer NEVER expires on its own, and his fourth stack is not a brief freeze but a Glacial Hold: the pile stays at 4 for as long as he holds the enemy (only an enemy mender's Cleansing Rite thaws it, a stack at a time, and never breaks the hold), and drops to one lingering stack only when he releases it, so the next build starts warm.

short: Frozen solid: skips turns until the ice thaws.
long: A frozen unit loses its turns until the freeze expires (it thaws one step during each skipped turn). Freezing comes from stacking Chilled to 4, or outright from the Cryomancer's Glacial Prison. Bosses are immune unless Broken. A freeze the CRYOMANCER causes is different: it never expires at all, except on a boss, which shrugs it off after {=Battle.ORDINARY_FREEZE_TURNS} turn - see Glacial Hold.

short: The Cryomancer's freeze: indefinite, until he ends it, he falls, or a Harvest or Cull purges it.
long: The Cryomancer's passive. Four stacks of his Chilled put an enemy in a HOLD rather than a brief freeze: it leaves the turn order entirely and stays there INDEFINITELY. Nothing thaws it by accident - not damage from your allies, not his own Blizzard, not the passing of turns, not an enemy Cleansing Rite. It ends when he ends it: Ice Lance on the held enemy, the drafted Shatter (which breaks every hold at once), or a new freeze past his limit, which frees the oldest. It also ends if he falls or a hero's Harvest or Cull purges the enemy's afflictions, and a cell of the Glass Prison rune shatters under any damage. He holds ONE enemy; Cryoclasm moves a hold to a different enemy without spending it. A held enemy takes +{=Battle.HOLD_WINDOW}% damage from every hero's strike, so the hold is a damage window as well as a lockdown - a HERO's window: the multiplier is read in the hero strike loop only, and a companion's jaws never see it. A released enemy comes back on {=Battle.HOLD_RELEASE_STACKS} stack of Chilled. GLACIAL PRISON IS REFUSED ONCE EVERY ENEMY IN FRONT OF YOU IS FROZEN: the ice is already as deep as it goes, so the button greys out rather than spending the turn on nothing. While any enemy is still free the button stays lit, so aim it at a free one. BOSSES: they resist the freeze until Broken, and a held boss shrugs the ice off after one turn.

short: Two enemies chained together: Chill on one lands on both, and damage echoes at {=Battle.FROSTBIND_SHARE*100}%.
long: A bond links two ENEMIES to each other. While it holds, Chilled applied to either partner is applied to the other as well, and damage dealt to one is dealt to the other at {=Battle.FROSTBIND_SHARE*100}%. Two rules make it readable. THE MIRRORED BLOW DOES NOT MIRROR BACK - the partner's share is not itself passed on, so a bond can never trade a blow back and forth between two bodies. AND A BOND IS NOT A HOLD: it grants the Cryomancer no extra prison. What it gives him is a second body that suffers with the first, so if both partners reach four stacks of Chilled the pair freezes together - and a bound pair then occupies ONE of his hold slots rather than two, which is how a Cryomancer limited to a single prison comes to hold two. Cleansing the bond from either partner breaks it for both.

short: Healing received reduced by 50%.
long: Frostbitten flesh knits badly: all healing this unit receives is halved while it lasts.

short: Fire damage at each turn start; reapplying extends it.
long: A burning unit takes fire damage at the start of each of its turns - about {=Battle.DOT_STATUSES.burn}% of the applier's Attack, locked in when the burn lands. Burn is fire-typed: fire resists shrink the ticks and fire vulnerability feeds them. Reapplying Burn ADDS duration rather than resetting it, so a fire build can keep a target lit indefinitely. The duration otherwise counts down one turn at a time; the Pyromancer's SLOW BURN stops that countdown on every enemy for four turns without stopping the damage, so the fire burns exactly as hard and simply does not get shorter, and his STOKE doubles what is left on one target.

short: Burn and Chilled, joined: each Burn tick also deals Break damage.
long: Burn and Chilled JOINED into one status - a second-degree Conjunction. It forms the moment either lands on a body already carrying the other, in either order, and it shows as one chip where two stood. It ticks when the Burn would, for the Burn's own damage, and deals Break damage with that same tick. It still burns and still slows: every card that asks whether the body is Burning or Chilled still finds both, and the chill's stacks still count. It lasts only as long as the SHORTER of the two would have; when that one runs out, the other stands alone again with what it had left. A cleanse lifts the whole Rupture as one status - but an enemy mender's Cleansing Rite only thaws its chill a stack at a time, as it thaws any chill, so the Rupture stands until that chill's last stack goes and the Burn then stands alone. A card that eats the Burn away entirely - Detonation does - leaves the Chill standing alone; one that only skims some of its turns leaves the Rupture standing.

short: Stacking nature damage at each turn start, skipping the first after it lands.
long: Each poison stack ticks for about {=Battle.DOT_STATUSES.poison}% of the applier's Attack at the victim's turn start, and stacks have no cap - the pile grows, and each new stack refreshes the timer. Poison is nature-typed, so nature resists blunt it.

short: Buildup meter: at 100 the target bleeds out for 20% max HP.
long: Wounding attacks add Bleed buildup (0-100). The meter never decays - it only climbs - and at 100 the target BLEEDS OUT: an immediate 20% of its max HP, ignoring armor and dealing no Break, after which the meter resets and builds again.

short: -{=Unit.SUNDER_STEP*100}% armor.
long: Sundered armor protects {=Unit.SUNDER_STEP*100}% less while the status lasts. It multiplies with a Break's -30%, so a Broken, Sundered target keeps less than half its armor.

short: Must attack the taunter.
long: A mocked enemy can only aim its attacks at whoever taunted it - the Warrior's Mocking Blow and the bear's Guardian's Roar both force the fight onto the sturdiest ally on the field.

short: Takes 15% more damage.
long: An exposed unit takes 15% more damage from every strike while the status lasts - an attack or an ability that hits it. Damage over time, a sprung trap, a Ruin detonation, a companion's blow and the abilities that deal their own separate damage are not raised.

short: -25% damage dealt.
long: A crippled unit deals 25% less damage with every strike until it fades; the damage over time it lays is not reduced.

short: -15% damage dealt, for the rest of the battle.
long: A hexed unit deals 15% less damage with every strike (not with the damage over time it lays), and it never fades - the hex lasts as long as the battle does. It is the Cursed Visage's whole payload: one item, no turn spent, every living enemy hexed at once. That reach is why the number is small where Cripple's is large; permanent and universal is worth far more than deep and brief, and the two stack when both land. Hexed is a debuff, so a Survivalist's Trapper counts it and a mender's Cleansing Rite could take it off an enemy - but a Mage's Dispel never can, which is what keeps the heroes' own hundred gold of work from being stripped back off by their own spell.

short: Attacks are 20% more likely to miss.
long: A dazed unit's single-target attacks miss an extra 20% of the time, on top of the {=Battle.MISS_CHANCE*100}% base; its area attacks and counters never miss.

short: Attacks are 50% more likely to miss.
long: Blinded single-target attacks miss an extra 50% of the time - most of what this unit swings at one target, it will not hit; its area attacks still never miss.

short: Charmed: strikes its own allies, dazing them.
long: A bewitched unit turns on its own side, basic-attacking its allies and Dazing them with every strike. Bosses REFUSE it outright until they are BROKEN - the key is the Break meter, so grind it down first.

short: 50% each turn to act against its own side.
long: Madness: each turn there is a 50% chance the unit turns on its own - attacking a fellow, or casting its helpful magic on the enemy side. Bosses REFUSE it outright until they are BROKEN - the key is the Break meter, so grind it down first.

retired: RETIRED at BATCH GG — kept, and said to be kept. Nothing in the game can apply Decay: its two appliers are talent riders, Empowered Hex on Hex of Ruin and Lingering Torment as a madness ends, and each reads a talent field that nothing has written since Batch FX replaced the twelve spec trees with one. LOST: the Decay entry in the glossary panel. KEPT: this entry's text, the status id, its chip and its turn-start Break tick. Deleting this string brings the entry back, and it is owed back the day anything applies Decay again.
short: 10 Break damage at the start of each turn.
long: Rot eats at the will: a decaying unit takes 10 Break damage at each of its turn starts, marching its own meter toward a Break with no further help.

short: Marked {=Battle.OLD_GODS_MARK} per debuff: +2% damage taken per stack; no cap, and it does not wear off.
long: The Occultist's debuffs mark enemies with {=Battle.OLD_GODS_MARK} Ruin apiece, and the mark lasts: it has NO MAXIMUM, it DOES NOT WEAR OFF, and it survives its own detonation. Only a few things take it away - an enemy mender's Cleansing Rite, a hero's Harvest or Cull, the Occultist's own Requiem and Transference (which moves it to another enemy), and the Open Wound rune, which wears it down a stack a turn. Each stack is +2% damage taken, and each stack deepens the draught heroes drink when they strike it - 2% of the damage dealt per stack, capped at {=Battle.RUIN_LEECH_CAP*100}% however many stacks and talents pile up. Every TENTH stack the mark is primed and DETONATES when the victim next acts: shadow damage off the Occultist's Attack, and the heroes are mended by the Old Gods' feast. The stacks SURVIVE the blast, so the next one waits for the next multiple of ten.

short: Next turn: strikes a fellow with double Break damage.
long: The maddened unit spends its next turn striking one of its own with DOUBLE Break damage, Sundering them in the bargain. Bosses REFUSE it outright until they are BROKEN - the key is the Break meter, so grind it down first.

short: Branded: half of most strikes it takes echoes to its whole warband.
long: A branded unit becomes a conduit: half the damage of every strike it takes echoes out to every member of its warband - a companion's blow, damage over time and the abilities that deal their own separate damage do not echo. Focus fire on the sigil and the whole warband pays.

short: Elemental resistances reduced.
long: Magic Burst leaves it for {=Battle.ELEM_WEAK_TURNS} turns: the victim's resistance to every school but Physical is lowered by {=Battle.ELEM_WEAK_PCT}%, so each of those schools lands harder - a resisted one is shrugged off less, and a weakness bites deeper still. It deepens an attack or an ability that strikes the victim. Damage over time, a sprung trap, a Ruin detonation and the abilities that deal their own separate damage are not deepened.

short: Armor permanently burned away.
long: Armor burned away for the rest of the battle - a small permanent reduction that keeps deepening while the target burns. NOTE: nothing in the game applies this today. Batch AR re-specced the Pyromancer talent that did, and the status is kept the way a vaulted ability is kept, so a later batch can point something at it again.

short: A trap waits: next action springs a stun and poison.
long: A Hunter's trap waits underfoot: the next time this enemy acts, the trap springs - it is Stunned for a turn and Poisoned. A SNARE IS SET UNDER ONE ENEMY AND SPRINGS ONCE; a Deadfall is untargeted, takes whoever acts next, and springs four times over a fight with two turns of rest between.

short: Cannot be healed.
long: The trap's teeth hold the wound open: this unit cannot be healed at all - potions, spells, and regeneration all fail while it lasts. NOTE: nothing in the game applies this today. The Survivalist talent that did went with the twelve talent trees, and the status is kept so a later tree, rune or card can point at it again.

short: All abilities act 50% faster.
long: The Sharpshooter's Quick Draw hastens its bearer by 50% for several turns - every ability's next turn arrives sooner on the timeline. One of the boss-trophy abilities.

short: Every attack carries one damage type; resists and weaknesses key off it.
long: Every ability's damage belongs to one of seven schools: Physical, Fire, Frost, Nature, Shadow, Arcane, and Holy; a Bomb, a sigil's echo and a few follow-up hits carry none and read no resistance. Most enemies resist some schools and are vulnerable to others - the same Fireball can be shrugged off by one warband and ruin another. Scouting a fight node on the map shows the warband's identity ('Resists / Soft to'); hovering a unit in battle shows its exact percentages.

short: The steel school - most weapon attacks.
long: The default school: swords, arrows, claws. Few enemies resist it outright and none are very soft to it - physical damage is reliable but rarely finds a weakness to exploit.

short: The Pyromancer's school; Burn ticks are fire-typed.
long: Fire burns twice: the hit itself, and the Burn it so often leaves behind - Burn ticks check fire resistance too. Fire is the counter the forest fears.

short: The Cryomancer's school of Chill and Freeze.
long: Frost trades raw numbers for control: many of its cards Chill, and stacked Chill freezes. Several ranged enemy kinds are soft to it.

short: The Survivalist's school; Poison ticks are nature-typed.
long: Venom, thorn, and rot. Poison ticks check nature resistance, so a nature-resistant enemy blunts a poison build twice - and forest wardens resist it heavily.

short: The Occultist's school of hexes and Ruin.
long: The Old Gods' school: hexes and Ruin detonations. A good share of the wilds' brutes and shamans are soft to shadow.

short: The Arcanist's school of raw magic.
long: Raw magical force, fed by Resonance. Armored line-holders - shieldmasters and chiefs - tend to be soft to arcane where steel fails.

short: The Cleric's rare school of smites.
long: The rarest school - a handful of Cleric smites carry it. Little in the wilds resists the light.

short: Resists shrink a school's damage; vulnerabilities amplify it.
long: A resistance removes that fraction of incoming damage of its school BEFORE armor is applied - 50% frost resist halves every frost hit. A vulnerability is the same dial pushed negative: 'Vulnerable: Fire +25%' means every fire hit lands 25% harder. Armor then reduces what remains (never beyond 85%), and every hit that connects deals at least 1 damage. Warband resists are worth scouting on the map before you commit to the fight.

short: The Warrior's fuel: builds in the fight, spent on his heaviest blows.
long: Warriors start every battle at 0 Rage (cap 100) and build it by fighting: +5 at each turn start, +10 every time they are hit, and more from rage-generating attacks like Strike. Their strongest abilities spend it. A Warrior who has been in the thick of it longest hits the hardest.

short: The casters' pool: regenerates slowly, restored by potions and by a zone boss that opens a new zone.
long: Mage, Cleric, and Hunter abilities spend Mana (cap 100). It regenerates +12 at each turn start (the Mage's Evocation nearly doubles that), and potions refill it between fights - a relic that restores Mana on victory reaches every hero who spends it, the Hunter included - and a zone boss restores it in full when it opens the next zone (the last zone's boss, which the end boss follows on the same board, does not). Unlike Rage it carries over between battles - a drained Cleric stays drained until the heroes recover.

short: The Arcanist's stacks: no practical cap, no decay, and compounding both ways.
long: Damaging casts build Resonance - 1 per cast, 2 on a crit - and it has no practical maximum: the meter stops at 99. It does not decay, and nothing resets it before the battle ends. The bonuses COMPOUND rather than scaling per stack: at N stacks the damage bonus is {=Unit.RESONANCE_DMG_STEP}% x N(N+1)/2 and the damage TAKEN penalty is {=Unit.RESONANCE_TAKEN_STEP}% x N(N+1)/2, both uncapped, plus a flat +1% crit chance per stack. So 5 stacks is +22% damage and +11% taken; 8 is +54%/+27%; 12 is +117%/+59%; 16 is +204%/+102%. That curve IS the Arcanist - nothing early, everything late: at five stacks he is weaker than a flat per-stack ramp would make him, and by twelve he has roughly doubled while taking half again as much. THREE cards take Resonance away and all three must be EARNED - he starts with none, and they are deliberately different shapes. STABILIZE (a boss-pool pick) VENTS everything above 2 for Mana and a short damage shield: the escape hatch from the escalation. ARCANE BOLT (a draft card) spends it as damage - 15% of Attack per stack, and then HALVES what he holds, so the curve keeps compounding from where it lands instead of restarting. THRESHOLD (a draft card) SETS the meter to {=Battle.THRESHOLD_STACKS}: a jump from below, and from above an emergency that takes stacks away. One is a way out, one is a change of slope, and one is the late game bought early.

short: The Holy cleric's stacks, earned when heroes fall into danger.
long: Whenever any hero drops below half health, the Holy cleric gains a stack of Mercy (cap 5). Each held stack adds +5% to her healing (not to Consecration's drip or a revive) and takes {=Battle.MERCY_TAKEN_PER_STACK*100}% off each blow that strikes her (not off damage over time), and stacks are the fuel for Empowering casts. Mercy rewards the healer who waits for the moment of need.

short: Mercy is paid for CROSSING below half health, once - and at the cap the stack is simply lost.
long: Mercy has two edges and both are easy to meet without ever being told about them. THE FIRST IS THAT IT PAYS FOR A CROSSING, NOT FOR A STATE: a hero earns the Holy cleric a stack at the moment they fall below half of their maximum health, and never again while they stay there. Heroes already bloodied are heroes paying her nothing. THE SECOND EDGE IS THE CAP: she holds at most 5, and a stack earned while she is full is thrown away entirely. The drafted ALMS catches it, turning the wasted stack into a ward on the hero who earned it. The drafted DIVINE PRESENCE answers the first edge from the other side: it pays her {=Battle.DIVINE_PRESENCE_MERCY} Mercy on every second turn of hers on which nobody crossed at all, which is exactly the turn the passive leaves her empty - and two stacks arriving together can cross the cap from below, which is what hands the spare one to Alms. The drafted VESPERS catches the blow that would take an ally below the line - up to {=Battle.VESPERS_PCT*100}% of HER maximum health, once - and a crossing that never happens earns her nothing; a bigger blow still crosses.

short: Spend a Mercy stack to supercharge the next Holy cast.
long: The Holy cleric can arm an Empower (C in battle), spending 1 Mercy to supercharge the next Heal, Renewal, Hymn, Resurrection, or Divine Plea - Resurrection, for one, returns the fallen at FULL health. An Empowered cast forgoes its Perfect skill-check bonus; the surge replaces finesse.

short: The Devout's gift: stacks that grow on shielded heroes and on holy ground, and pay off the deepest count you have held.
long: Faith lives mostly on the Devout's fellow HEROES - but he carries it too, and HIS never releases: his count holds at {=Battle.FAITH_RELEASE}, paying him exactly what it pays everyone else. Two things build it for everyone: every hit a Divine Shield absorbs builds TWO stacks on its bearer, and every hero standing on Consecrated Ground gains one at the start of their turn (cap {=Battle.FAITH_RELEASE}). WHAT A STACK IS WORTH IS PAID ON THE HIGHEST COUNT YOU HAVE HELD THIS BATTLE, not on the count you hold right now - so a release never takes the benefit away, and Faith is a high-water mark rather than a balance. Each of those stacks grants {=Battle.FAITH_MITIGATION_PCT}% damage reduction and +{=Battle.FAITH_DAMAGE_PCT}% damage dealt. At {=Battle.FAITH_RELEASE} a HERO'S Faith releases - a heal of 15%+ max HP - and the COUNT resets to build again while the high-water mark stands. At two stacks an absorbed hit, a release comes roughly every fourth absorbed hit. The builders are drips rather than bursts on purpose - a shielded hero HOLDS what one absorbed hit gives him, and holding is what the high-water mark is for. A builder large enough to fill the bar in one event would delete the held half of the meter. Every release also makes the Devout himself a little bigger: his maximum health rises {=Battle.CONVICTION_GROWTH_PCT*100}% for the rest of the battle and he is healed for the same amount, so the more his shields are tested, the more there is to shield with. The high-water mark is per-battle: the next fight opens at zero.

short: The Sharpshooter's aim: builds on one target, lost on switching.
long: Every attack on the SAME target builds +20 Focus and THE METER HAS NO CEILING; switching targets dumps it to zero, and a kill banks up to 50 toward the next mark. THE PAYOFF CONVERTS AT {=Unit.FOCUS_CONVERT}: the first {=Unit.FOCUS_CONVERT} points each grant +{=Unit.FOCUS_STEP*100}% critical chance, and every point beyond {=Unit.FOCUS_CONVERT} grants +{=Unit.FOCUS_STEP*100}% of critical MULTIPLIER instead - so Lethal Aim's x2.5 becomes x3 at 200 Focus and x3.5 at 300, and it never stops paying. Patience buys certainty first, then force. Coup de Grace spends the whole meter but reads at most {=Battle.COUP_FOCUS_CAP} points of it. HIS BASIC ATTACK IS ALSO A FOCUS ENGINE IN ITS OWN RIGHT: it runs a multi-press skill check that grows with the Focus he already holds - one press, plus one per {=Battle.SS_SEQ_STEP} Focus, capped at four - and pays {=Battle.SS_SEQ_FOCUS_PER_PRESS} Focus a landed press plus {=Battle.SS_SEQ_FULL_BONUS} for a full sequence, on top of the +20 above. The deeper the meter, the faster it fills.

short: The Beastmaster's passive: each active companion grants its own boon.
long: Every companion the Beastmaster fields grants a boon that scales with its Loyalty - Ursus draws enemy attacks and blunts what reaches the hunter, Canis sharpens him against wounded prey, Aguila lifts every hero's crit chance. The boon is x(1 + 0.20 per Loyalty stack) and it has no ceiling. PAST {=Battle.BOND_CONVERT} LOYALTY THE METER CONVERTS AND THIS IS THE HALF THAT RECEIVES: a stack past the point stops adding to the companion's strike damage and feeds this boon instead, so it grows at double the step above {=Battle.BOND_CONVERT}. HE FIELDS ONE COMPANION AT A TIME.

short: The Pyromancer is paid for every turn of Burn standing on the enemy team.
long: The Pyromancer has no bar of his own - his power is the FIRE ALREADY ON THE BOARD. Two clauses. BONUS: he deals +{=Battle.OVERBURN_STEP}% more damage for every remaining turn of Burn standing across the whole enemy team, up to +{=Battle.OVERBURN_CAP}%. One enemy burning for six turns feeds him exactly as hard as six burning for one. REFUND: every turn of Burn he CONSUMES hands him back 1 Mana - Detonation, Wildfire, Cinderfall, Ember Debt, Funeral Pyre and Pyre Wake all pay it, because the refund belongs to the passive rather than to any one ability. HOLDING FIRE COSTS HIM NOTHING. What makes him a commitment spec is that his damage is DEFERRED: Burn ticks are small, Detonation pays 250% of the bank it empties, and turns spent lighting fires are turns not spent killing - he is weak until he cashes in.

short: Every enemy shows what it is about to do, and it can be denied.
long:
Each enemy picks its next action the moment its turn ends - and every enemy picks once before the first turn of a fight - then shows that choice until it acts. The icon appears twice: under the enemy's portrait in the turn bar (on its next turn's slot only) and on its nameplate, where it is written out. Seven categories: Strike (single-target damage), Sweep (an attack that hits every ally or several of them), Crush (a blow whose Break damage is greater than its damage's percentage of Attack), Afflict (applies a status, and the status is named), Bolster (buffs, wards or cleanses its own side), Mend (heals) and Wind-up (a charged blow landing on a later turn, with the turns remaining).

HOVER THE INTENT FOR ITS NUMBERS: the ability's name, its damage band and Break damage, any status it lays, and how many heroes it hits. The band is the attack's own roll, before armor, resistance, Block and a critical - what the blow could be, never what it will deal.

A DECLARED ACTION CAN BE DENIED, and that is the point. Stun, Freeze, Break or hold the enemy and the announced action is DISCARDED - not saved for later, exactly as cancelling a wind-up has always worked. Hysteria, Bewitch and Psychosis take the turn the same way. Two softer cases: kill the target it named and it re-targets WITH THE SAME ABILITY (the plan holds, only the victim changes); leave it unable to pay for the ability and it falls back to its basic attack, and the combat log says so rather than substituting in silence.

short: The Beastmaster's bond, built per companion, uncapped, lost with it.
long: Each living companion builds Loyalty at the hunter's turn start, and there is NO CEILING on it. Every stack is +5% companion strike damage plus that companion's own gift, and the Pack Bond boon itself climbs continuously with the meter - x(1 + 0.20 per stack), so x2 at five, and it never plateaus. PAST {=Battle.BOND_CONVERT} STACKS THE METER CONVERTS: the first {=Battle.BOND_CONVERT} buy the companion's strike damage, and every stack past {=Battle.BOND_CONVERT} stops adding to the strike and feeds the Pack Bond boon instead - so the boon climbs at double its step above the point (x3.4 at ten, x7.4 at twenty) while the strike step holds at what {=Battle.BOND_CONVERT} stacks bought. A converted stack is paid in full - into the boon, or, once Ursus's boon has given all it can, back into the strike step. The four cards that spend the RAW stack count - Unleash, Primal Surge, Last Howl and Bring It Down - and all three companion gifts are untouched by the split, because it changes what a stack PAYS and they count stacks. A companion's death wipes its Loyalty - the bond dies with it, and that is the whole stake of the partnership.

short: The Occultist's meter lives on the enemy, as Ruin stacks.
long: The Occultist has no bar of their own - their power accumulates on ENEMIES as stacks of Ruin - {=Battle.OLD_GODS_MARK} for every debuff they apply - with no ceiling and no expiry. See the Ruin status for what the mark does and how it detonates.

short: One tree of twenty-seven nodes in three tiers of nine, bought per CLASS.
long: There is ONE talent tree, and every class buys into it out of its own purse - a Berserker, a Warden and a Swordmaster all spend the Warrior's points in the same twenty-seven nodes. The nodes sit in three TIERS of nine, and within a tier there are no lanes, no rows and no prerequisites: you buy what you can afford. Every node is a stat or a rule the battle already reads - none of them touches a rune, an ability or a passive - and no node grants an ability.

short: A cell costs its tier: tier 1 costs {=Talents.TIER_COSTS.0} point, tier 2 costs {=Talents.TIER_COSTS.1}, tier 3 costs {=Talents.TIER_COSTS.2}.
long: Buying a cell costs its tier: tier 1 cells cost {=Talents.TIER_COSTS.0} point, tier 2 cost {=Talents.TIER_COSTS.1}, tier 3 cost {=Talents.TIER_COSTS.2}. Twenty-seven cells is 54 POINTS TO FILL THE TREE FOR ONE CLASS, which at {=Run.SLOT_COUNT} points a completed run is eighteen completions. Points are freely reassignable between runs at no cost - respec the whole class and spend them again - and never during a run.

short: Earned per class, per zone boss, and banked forever. A run pays none.
long: Talent points are PERMANENT META PROGRESSION. You earn 1 PER CLASS PER ZONE BOSS DEFEATED - three zone bosses, so 3 a class for a completed run, and a run that dies in zone 2 still banks 1, or in zone 3, 2. Only the classes among your heroes earn, and every spec of a class spends that class's purse. Points are per class and never transfer, and they bank without limit. NOTHING IN A RUN AWARDS ONE: fights, elites and mini-bosses pay gold and their own spoils, and the END BOSS pays a relic. Spent between runs on the Talents screen.

short: Each zone boss grants every hero a new ability, from their spec pool first.
long: Felling a zone boss lets EVERY hero claim a trophy: one new ability, offered as a pick on that hero's card on the map - from their own spec's pool, and once that is spent, from their draft pools. All twelve specs carry a pool, two to five abilities deep. The end boss instead leaves a relic and gold - the run's final prize.

short: Every mini-boss hands each hero one; the blacksmith sells more.
long: Clearing a MINI-BOSS awards every hero an ability upgrade - a pick of three, resolved on that hero's map card. An upgrade is a permanent change to ONE ability the hero already owns, and it lasts the rest of the run. There are eight: HONED (+50% damage), QUICKENED (-2 turns of cooldown, minimum 0), EFFORTLESS (costs no Rage or Mana - Mercy and Focus are unaffected), SWIFT (arrives 25% sooner, never below {=Ability.DELAY_FLOOR} initiative - half the setup cap), WEIGHTED (Break damage doubled), WIDENED (one more target, or one more hit), PIERCING (ignores half the target's armor) and CERTAIN (its status application always lands). Three mini-bosses a run means three upgrades per hero, twelve across the four - and the BLACKSMITH sells more on top of that, for gold. Upgrades STACK on a single ability - one ability can end a run Honed and Swift at once - but the SAME upgrade never comes twice to the same hero from a mini-boss. (The blacksmith is not that pool: it will sell you a second Honed for a different ability, and buying one never uses up a mini-boss pick.) They apply LAST, after talents and after equipped runes, so an upgrade always wins over a talent that sets the same field. You are only ever offered an upgrade that has something to change: Honed is never offered on a heal, Effortless never on a free ability, Weighted never on something that deals no Break damage, Widened never on a single-hit attack (nor on an area attack, which already hits everything), Certain never on a status that already always lands, and Swift never on an ability already sitting at the {=Ability.DELAY_FLOOR} initiative floor. Because three are drawn from eight, any one upgrade turns up about half as often as it used to - a hero can finish a run having never been offered the one their build wanted, which is the variety working rather than a fault. An upgraded ability wears a gold up-arrow on its button in battle and on its row in the loadout panel; hovering it names the upgrades.

short: Every combat win makes every hero permanently stronger this run.
long: Each battle won grants every hero +2% of their base Attack and HP for the rest of the run. Enemies climb their own ladder - roughly +2% Attack and +2.5% HP per slot, with a hard jump between zones - so the heroes and the map rise together, and every slot fought feeds the curve. A route that takes more fights arrives stronger; a route that takes fewer arrives sooner.

short: This run's gear: three slots per hero, eight held, and the Crest's bag.
long: Runes are equippable power for a single hero - or, worn in the Crest, for all four. One DROPS after every fight won - random, and always a rune for one of the four heroes' classes or a crest rune for all four. A rune for a class goes to the hero of that class, who HOLDS it unworn until he equips it - eight held at most, beside his slots - and a mark on his nameplate on the map counts the runes he holds and does not wear; the map names him when one drops. A crest rune goes into the BAG, which holds the Crest's runes, six at most. The Peddler sells runes too, though never a core rune, and an elite leaves a cache of three to choose from; each goes to its hero the same way. Equipping is its own act, from a hero's card (though a rune picked from a cache, a bargain or an event goes straight into a free slot, unless it is a core rune): a rune taken off stays with him, so a hero holding eight refuses an Unequip until one is dropped or sold - and a SWAP, one rune each way, always works - except a core-rune swap that would put Summon Companion back into a kit with no free slot. A rune that arrives for a hero holding eight, or for a full bag, is shown beside them: drop one of them to take it, or leave it behind. Every hero carries three slots from the run's start. CORE RUNES are the other kind, and each wears (core) after its name: each carries a rule that changes how a hero fights for the whole run, and belongs to one class. At class selection each hero is dealt three of the class's core runes and takes one; more are found in play - a drop or a cache, never the Peddler - and each waits with the hero, unworn, until it is slotted, into one of three core slots that sit apart from his three rune slots. A hero's rune panel lists his runes in three sections - his core slots, every one drawn, then the runes he wears, then every rune he holds and does not wear. Unequipping a core rune takes its rule, and the abilities that rule needs, out of the next fight; the hero keeps the rune, unworn. THE CREST is a slot of its own, beside the heroes' slots, for a CREST RUNE - a rune worn by every hero at once, which belongs to no class, drops and sells as any other rune does, and waits in the bag while the Crest does not wear it. A shop row, an event and the bag say it is for the crest; a hero's own pick of three - an elite's cache, a bargain's rune - never holds one. Some crest runes pay only while the heroes stand a certain way - while no Cleric stands, while a hero lies fallen - and switch on and off during a fight as heroes fall and are raised; the combat log says each time. Because such a rune pays only while its condition holds, it pays more than a rune that always pays. Every ordinary rune belongs to one CLASS and is offered to every hero of it, except that a rune reading a core rune's rule is offered only while that core rune is equipped, a rune that changes a named ability only to a hero who has that ability, and a rune that needs a companion only while no equipped core rune dismisses the pet. Nothing the heroes already hold is offered again, and a rune the game cannot pay is never offered. The class is what the shop row names beside a rune. There are no rarity tiers and no quality ladder: a rune found in the first zone is drawn from the same pool as one found in the last, and what a rune does is in its own text rather than in a grade. Some runes charge for their upside, and the cost is always written in the text. Runes vanish with the run. Every rune costs 150 gold, flat - price does not signal power, so you pay for FIT rather than for magnitude - and the Peddler buys back any rune nobody wears for a third.

short: Real power with a cost carved in - and the cost is in the text.
long: Some runes buy a larger upside with a real drawback - a companion that can no longer be healed, a hero who can no longer Block, a missed press that drains Focus. They wear no special name and no special colour: a rune that gives and takes is simply what that rune does, and the cost is always written in its own text. Read them twice; some are worth wearing anyway.

short: Relics outlive the run; runes die with it.
long: The two are easy to confuse and could not be more different. RELICS are permanent: every zone boss you fell unlocks one FOREVER, and at the draft you choose up to 3 unlocked relics to carry - effects that pay every hero, for the whole run. RUNES are of the run: bought and found along the way, worn by one hero (or, in the Crest, by all four), and gone the moment the run ends - by death or by victory. When you wipe, the relic you unlocked stays; the runes you were wearing do not.

short: The heroes' shared pouch: eight kinds of item, all usable in battle and two on the map.
long: Eight kinds of item, shared by all four heroes and carried in the pouch's slots (see Pouch Slots). In battle press ALT or use the Items action: a Health Potion restores {=Run.HEALTH_POTION_PCT*100}% of one hero's maximum health; a Mana Potion {=Run.MANA_POTION_PCT*100}% of one hero's maximum Mana or Rage; a Bomb deals {=Run.BOMB_BASE_DAMAGE} damage to every enemy, {=Run.BOMB_WIN_SCALE*100}% more for each victory this run; a Revive Potion raises a fallen hero at 50% health; a Defense Potion gives every living hero +10% armor for 3 turns; a Cleansing Draught removes every debuff from one hero but Broken, Bleed and a poison that refuses every cleanse; a Cursed Visage hexes every living enemy for the rest of the battle; and a Resonating Hourglass sends one hero to the front of the turn order. No one deals a bomb's damage and no one lays a potion's status — the pouch belongs to all four heroes: a bomb marks nothing, feeds nothing and claims no kill, and a Defense Potion's armor or a Cursed Visage's hex is no hero's to lengthen. Health and Mana Potions work on the map too, where a Mana Potion refills Mana and not Rage. Shops, elite spoils, bargains and some events refill the pouch.

short: Three zones, each a generated {=Run.SLOTS_PER_ZONE}-slot map to its boss.
long: A run is three zones and 49 encounters - sixteen to a zone, and the end boss. Each zone is a GENERATED MAP, not a road: {=Run.SLOTS_PER_ZONE} slots deep and three rows wide, branching from slot 1 to slot {=Run.MINI_SLOT}, converging on the MINI-BOSS at slot 8, branching again to slot {=Run.BOSS_SLOT}, and converging on the ZONE BOSS at slot {=Run.SLOTS_PER_ZONE}. You walk one node per column - {=Run.BRANCH_COLUMNS} free encounters plus the two that everything funnels into. Enemies grow with every slot and take a hard step up each zone; killing a zone's boss fully restores the heroes and sends you into the next zone. After the third zone's boss the END BOSS waits in a seventeenth slot, and its death ends the run in victory.

short: Fight, Elite, Smith, Trade and ??? - three ways forward, hover to scout.
long: Five kinds stand on the map. FIGHT nodes are battles, and each one won drops a rune for one of the heroes - hover one to scout its warband and what it resists. ELITE nodes are harder fights with the best rewards on the board. SMITH is the blacksmith, who sells one ability upgrade for gold. TRADE is the Peddler, with potions and runes. ??? is an event, and it does not say which kind it is until you are standing on it. The MINI-BOSS at slot 8 and the BOSS at slot {=Run.SLOTS_PER_ZONE} are unavoidable; everything else is a route you chose. NOTHING IS GUARANTEED ON A ROUTE. A zone holds {=Run.NODE_COPIES.elite} elites, {=Run.NODE_COPIES.blacksmith} smiths, {=Run.NODE_COPIES.merchant} peddlers and {=Run.NODE_COPIES.event} events - and the first zone keeps every smith and peddler out of the run's first three steps, where the gold to use one is not there yet - but you walk {=Run.BRANCH_COLUMNS} nodes out of about 40 - route past every smith and you get no smith that zone. Edges only ever reach the same row or the one next to it and they never cross, so a step down closes the corridor above you for the next couple of columns. That is what makes a fork a decision instead of a detour.

short: The map's hardest fights short of its bosses - and its best paydays. Six stand in every zone.
long: Six ELITE nodes stand in every zone, never two in adjacent columns and never in column 1. You may not meet them all: how many a route takes is up to the route. Tougher warbands, always led by a chief. The payout is the run's snowball engine - 80-100 gold, a consumable, a draft pick for every living hero, and a rune cache where one hero picks from up to three runes. A bargain is offered at the door of every one. Skipping them all is a real option and a weak one: an elite you did not fight is a draft pick and a rune you do not have.

short: Buys one ability upgrade with gold. Six on the map, about two on your route.
long: A SMITH node sells ABILITY UPGRADES - the same eight the mini-boss awards, on the same abilities, with the same rules about what fits what. Three pairings on the counter, one hero each; you buy ONE and the visit is over. Gold only: no health cost, no second currency. The price scales with the zone - {=Run.BLACKSMITH_PRICES.0}, then {=Run.BLACKSMITH_PRICES.1}, then {=Run.BLACKSMITH_PRICES.2} - so late gold still has somewhere to go. An upgrade bought here does NOT use up a mini-boss pick, and it does not stop a mini-boss offering the same upgrade later: you may buy Honed twice in a run on two different abilities. Six smiths stand in every zone and a route walks about two, so a run that wants them has to be routed toward them; none stands in the run's first three steps.

short: A shop you can see coming, and plan to arrive at with gold.
long: The Peddler used to turn up after a won fight, about two fights in five. Now they stand on the map as a TRADE node - five a zone, about two on a route - so a shop is something you route toward with gold in hand rather than something that happens to you. The stock: potions, and one rune offered to every hero, held by him once bought (a crest rune goes to the bag) - never a rune the heroes already hold. The Peddler also buys back any rune nobody wears for a third of its price, and a hero holding eight refuses a purchase until one is sold. None stands in the run's first three steps. The only merchant that still follows a fight is the one a BARGAIN at the road's mildest severity pays out, and that one was bought with a modifier.

short: Three offers before every elite and mini-boss: a modifier plus a reward.
long: Before every ELITE and every MINI-BOSS - the mini-boss and every elite your route takes, and never a plain fight or a boss - the road stops and offers three bargains. Each is one MODIFIER plus one REWARD, both shown before you choose. There is no decline: one of the three is taken. The modifier is the price and binds the coming battle only; the reward pays ON VICTORY, which is why 'a merchant follows the fight' is a reward you have to earn rather than a shop you walk into. Lose the fight and you paid the price for nothing. The offer screen shows the warband you are about to face and your heroes' health alongside the three cards, because choosing a severity-4 bargain at 30% health should be a decision, not a surprise.

short: A condition binding BOTH parties for one battle.
long: A modifier is a rule change that holds for exactly one battle. THE TWENTY EVERY ROAD DEALS BIND BOTH SIDES - never just yours and never just theirs. Under Feverish everyone deals 25% more damage; under Bloodless nobody heals, on either side: a change to the fight, not a difficulty slider. RUIN'S FOUR bind one side - Famine, Wasting, the Hungering Dark and Cruel Order, severity {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.gamble_band.0}, dealt as Ruin's gambles and on no other road: the road leaning on your heroes, the harshest bargains in the game and the best paid. The twenty are weighted toward the mild end because the safe slot on Wanderer's and Warden's bargains draws from that end and is therefore what you see most. The modifier is stamped on every combatant when the fight begins - a companion summoned mid-battle is bound by it too - and it is gone the moment the fight ends.

short: 1-5: how harsh a modifier is, and what decides the reward.
long: Every modifier carries a severity of 1 to 5, shown as pips on its bargain card. The REWARD TABLE READS SEVERITY, NOT YOUR HEROES: a 1 pays 40 gold, a 2 pays 80 gold or a potion, a 3 pays 140 gold or a rune, a 4 pays 220 gold or a rune, a 5 pays 300 gold or a rune. A MERCHANT AFTER THE FIGHT is the reward of the mildest severity the road deals - a {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.wanderer.safe_band.0} on Wanderer and Warden, a {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.safe_band.0} on Ruin - which pays its own reward or the merchant. In the run's first {=Run.SHOP_GATE_NODES} steps, where no merchant is offered, it pays its own reward alone. Severity is FLAT and deliberately ignores your heroes: a modifier that happens to be cheap for your build is a good deal you earned by building that way, and a severity that read your heroes would quietly tax every build for being good at something. EVERY OFFER HOLDS ONE SAFE OPTION AND TWO GAMBLES, each dealt from its own band of severity, and the bands harden with the road: Wanderer deals its safe option from severity {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.wanderer.safe_band.0} to {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.wanderer.safe_band.1} and its gambles from {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.wanderer.gamble_band.0} to {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.wanderer.gamble_band.1}; Warden its safe option from {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.warden.safe_band.0} to {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.warden.safe_band.1} and its gambles at {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.warden.gamble_band.0} alone; Ruin its safe option from {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.safe_band.0} to {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.safe_band.1} and its gambles at {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.gamble_band.0} alone - on Ruin there is no mild option, and its gambles are four bargains no other road deals. The safe option is guaranteed by how the cards are dealt rather than by luck, so heroes on their last legs always have the mildest choice the road allows.

short: ??? - a trade, a gift, or a toll. You will not know which until you arrive.
long: Five ??? nodes stand in every zone, and all three kinds wear the same icon. Most are TRADEOFFS: two or three conversions of one resource into another - health for a rune, maximum health for gold - at a rate you take or decline, and DECLINING IS ALWAYS ONE OF THE BUTTONS. Some are BOONS, a straight gift at no cost. A few are BANES, a straight cost with nothing to choose. The three are indistinguishable on the map on purpose: a node that announced itself as a bane would simply never be walked onto. No bane can kill a hero or take anyone below 1 HP - it costs a resource, never a run.

short: All four down ends the run - relics, talents and the chronicle survive.
long: When every hero falls, the run is over: gold, runes, items, and the map are all lost. What lives on the profile survives every death - the RELICS you have unlocked (yours forever, pickable at the next draft), the TALENTS your classes have bought and the points they have banked, and the chronicle of cycles survived and lost. The run summary lays out how the attempt ended and what the heroes had built; the next climb starts wiser.

short: Three rungs - Wanderer, Warden and Ruin - chosen at the draft.
long: At the draft you choose the road, one of three rungs (see The Difficulty Ladder). WANDERER is the first: its enemies hit half as hard - all but the END BOSS - and it is where a profile with no talents belongs. WARDEN is the game as designed. RUIN makes the enemies {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.mult} times as strong, and its bargains harsher. Beating the END BOSS on a rung is what opens that tier of the talent tree.

short: A cell bought is a cell worn - there is no equip step.
long: BUYING a cell spends points and owns it until you respec - a free respec between runs clears a class's cells and refunds the points - and an owned cell is WORN: no node in the tree is exclusive, so there is nothing to choose between and no separate equip step. Every cell a class owns is on every hero of that class, every run, and it locks for the whole run the moment the spec is confirmed.

short: A tier opens by beating the END BOSS on its difficulty AND owning three cells of the tier below.
long: A fresh save has NO TIERS, no points and no talents at all. A tier has TWO GATES and needs both. THE DIFFICULTY GATE: beating the end boss on difficulty 1 opens tier {=Talents.TIERS_OPEN.1}, difficulty 2 opens tier {=Talents.TIERS_OPEN.2}, difficulty 3 opens tier {=Talents.TIERS_OPEN.3} - and it is GLOBAL, applying to every class at once, unlike points, which are per class. THE SPEND GATE: tier 2 opens for a class once it owns three tier-1 cells, and tier 3 once it owns three tier-2 cells. The build screen names which gate is shutting a tier, because one is fixed by winning and the other by buying.

short: Three rungs, chosen at the draft. Each above the first adds a named twist.
long: The road has three rungs. WANDERER is the opening rung, tuned below the rest so untalented heroes can meet it. WARDEN raises the enemies and HARDENS THE SAFE BARGAIN - the guaranteed mild option gets less mild. RUIN raises both again, so its safe option is never mild and its gambles are severity {=Run.DIFFICULTIES.ruin.gamble_band.0} - four bargains no other road deals - and adds the second twist: FIXED ENCOUNTERS CARRY A MODIFIER, so the mini-boss and every boss - the nodes a route cannot duck - fight under one, of severity {=Run.FIXED_MODIFIER_BAND.0} or {=Run.FIXED_MODIFIER_BAND.1}. Beating the END BOSS on a rung is what opens that tier of the talent tree, for every class at once.

short: A fourth boss after zone {=Run.SLOT_COUNT}. Awards a relic while any is locked, no points, and opens a talent tier.
long: Three ZONE BOSSES pay each class a talent point apiece; after the third zone stands THE END BOSS, the forty-ninth encounter. It is FIXED rather than drawn from a pool, so it can be learned, and it GAINS STATS AND MECHANICS WITH DIFFICULTY - a fourth ability at rung 2 and a fifth at rung 3. It unlocks a relic you do not have yet, while any is still locked. It awards NO talent points and no ability pick, because nothing follows it. What it does award is the talent tier matching the rung you beat it on.

short: The pouch holds a limited number of item KINDS: {=Run.ITEM_SLOTS_BY_ZONE.0}, then {=Run.ITEM_SLOTS_BY_ZONE.1}, then {=Run.ITEM_SLOTS_BY_ZONE.2}.
long: A slot holds one item TYPE and its whole stack - six Health Potions are one slot, not six. The heroes open with four slots and four kinds, and a slot is added on clearing each zone boss, to five and then six. Because items cost no turn, the shop used to ask only whether you could afford a thing; the slot cap turns that into what you make room for. A stack running to zero does NOT free its slot - only discarding it from the pouch, or selling it back at a merchant for a fraction of its price, releases one. A drop with nowhere to go is not refused: it is offered, and you choose what to give up or walk away. A stack that is simply FULL is still refused outright, which is a different thing. The three items added alongside the slots are battle-only and shop-priced against it: the Cleansing Draught ({=Run.ITEM_PRICES.cleanse}g, stacks to {=Run.ITEM_STACK_CAPS.cleanse}) strips every debuff from one hero but Broken, Bleed and a poison that refuses every cleanse and is the answer heroes without a Cleric never had; the Cursed Visage ({=Run.ITEM_PRICES.visage}g, stacks to {=Run.ITEM_STACK_CAPS.visage}) hexes every living enemy for the whole fight; the Resonating Hourglass ({=Run.ITEM_PRICES.hourglass}g, stacks to {=Run.ITEM_STACK_CAPS.hourglass}) pulls any living hero to the front of the queue. The last two never drop - shop-only, so what they cost is what they are worth.

short: New abilities offered three at a time by elites and events.
long: Beside the zone-boss pick sits a second, larger source of abilities. EVERY ELITE OFFERS ONE TO EVERY LIVING HERO ON VICTORY, and some EVENTS trade for one. EACH HERO DRAFTS ALONE, ON ONE SCREEN OF HIS OWN, which opens by itself when the heroes reach the map - one hero after another, in the order the picks were earned - and an elite's rune cache waits on the same screen as that hero's card. THE PEDDLER NO LONGER SELLS ONE: a draft pick is earned and never bought. Every offer is three cards the hero does not already own, drawn from his class's one draft pool. EACH HERO DRAWS FROM THEIR OWN POOLS - a Pyromancer is never shown a Warden card, and a hero who fell in the fight is back up before the screen opens and drafts like anyone else. If the pool cannot fill three it FILLS SHORT rather than repeating itself; a hero with nothing left to be shown is simply not offered one. Six elites stand in every zone, so how much you draft is a property of the road you walked: a greedy route drafts far more than a cautious one. DECLINING IS ALWAYS ALLOWED, PER HERO AND INDEPENDENTLY - one hero taking a card does not commit the others. A declined offer does not come back to that run's pool FOR THAT HERO; the ledger is per hero, so refusing a card for one never hides it from another. A card benched to make room is not refused: it stays the hero's, and can be carried again. A HERO'S SCREEN RESOLVES AS ONE ACTION: his card and his rune are chosen, then the screen is confirmed, so either can be reconsidered until then; Later leaves both waiting, marked on his card, and they open again the next time the heroes reach the map. At the slot cap - seven, and one more at every zone boss - the card does not resolve until you have named which card the incoming one benches.

short: Seven words that name what a card is for. Shown on the draft card.
long: Every ability in the game and every authored rune but the core runes carries one or two ARCHETYPE TAGS, and the draft card shows them under the card's name. A tag names what the card is FOR, in a vocabulary shared across the whole roster, so a choice between three cards can be read as a choice between three directions before a word of the description is read. THE SEVEN: DEBUFF - lands a harmful effect on an enemy, or spends one. DEFENSE - answers damage coming in: heals, absorbs or reduces it. BREAK - moves a Break meter. RESOURCE - moves Mana, Rage or a class meter. OFFENSE - raises the damage the holder deals. TEMPO - moves the initiative timeline or a cooldown. MARK - lays a lasting mark on one enemy. SEVEN IS THE CEILING: a tag only means something if holding two is notable, and every word added divides the corpus finer, so an eighth needs an argument. AT MOST TWO A CARD AND THE FIRST IS THE PRIMARY: what the card is for, with the second naming what it also touches. BREAK IS A SECONDARY ONLY: no card carries it first. It names a mechanic where the other six name a role, so it was demoted to make the primary vocabulary uniform - and demoted rather than removed, so a Break build is still readable on the card. So a card that Breaks as it hits reads OFFENSE first, with BREAK beside it. THE PROTECTED CORE ABILITIES CARRY THEM TOO, which is what gives a build a seed - a Pyromancer opens holding a DEBUFF card whether or not he ever drafts one. No ability, talent, relic or rune reads a tag: they are there for you to read, and the loadout panel counts them - both tags of every card you carry. NOTE that the same word ARCHETYPE also names a SPECIALIZATION's role - Ramp, Nuker, Warder and the rest, one per spec, which decides base Attack. A tag is a property of a CARD, not of a hero, and nothing reads both.

short: Cards written for a whole CLASS, drawn from its one pool beside its spec cards.
long: Every draft offer draws from ONE POOL, your CLASS's: the cards written for each of its specs and the CLASS-WIDE cards written for all of them, shuffled together with no share or slot for either - so a Pyromancer, a Cryomancer and an Arcanist can all be offered Mirror Image. They are deliberately UNTIED AND GENERAL: a class card would not read as off-theme for any spec of the class, which is why it is Mirror Image and not Frostbolt. AS WRITTEN THEY ARE WEAKER THAN SPEC ABILITIES - but unconditional. Most feed no passive - an illusion does nothing for Overburn, a blessing does nothing for Ruin - though the Rage a Warrior spends on one still fills Blood Frenzy. ALL FOUR CLASSES HAVE THEM - six Warrior and six Hunter cards, five Mage and three Cleric. Five cards that were class-wide are in the CLASS KITS now, guaranteed rather than drawn, and a hero who took a spine at class selection draws from the same class pool as everyone else.

short: A kit holds seven abilities, and every zone boss adds a slot. At the cap, taking one means benching one.
long: A hero's kit opens with room for SEVEN abilities and every zone boss adds one more, to ten - and the protected core counts against it, the class kit included, except the basic attack and a core rune's enablers, which take no slot: every hero opens with his class kit's 3 filled, and the Sharpshooter, who fields no companion, with 2. AT THE CAP AN OFFER BECOMES TAKE-ONE-AND-BENCH-ONE: you pick the incoming ability and then name which of your EARNED abilities it benches. Only earned abilities can be benched; the protected core never can. A benched ability stays yours and can be carried again between fights; only an offer you DECLINE is gone for the run. The cap binds every source alike - though a zone boss raises it before it awards its own pick, so that pick needs a bench only when a draft card taken on the same screen fills the new slot first.

short: The basic attack, the class kit, and whatever each held core rune needs to work.
long: Every hero keeps a PROTECTED CORE: the basic attack, the CLASS KIT - three abilities every hero of the class opens with, whatever core rune is held, save that a Lethal Aim holder opens without Summon Companion - and each held core rune's ENABLERS - the minimum abilities its rule cannot function without. Protected abilities CAN NEVER BE BENCHED, which is what stops the slot cap from breaking a core rune. An enabler travels with its core rune and takes no ability slot: a Mage holding the Rune of the Pyromancer (core) holds Flamewave, a Warrior holding the Rune of the Swordmaster (core) holds Guard Change, and unequipping the rune takes its enabler out of the next fight. The minimum varies by rune rather than following a rule: Overburn needs something that lays Burn, while Runaway Resonance builds on every damaging cast and brings nothing.

short: A temporary rise in your maximum health that decays - and current health clamps under it.
long: The Devout's Fortified Spirit lends an ally a share of HIS maximum health: their maximum rises by 30% of his (40% on a perfect cast) and they are healed for the same amount at once, so the new room arrives full rather than empty. THE LOAN THEN DECAYS - a tenth of his maximum is handed back at the start of each of that ally's turns, so 30% becomes 20%, then 10%, then nothing. CURRENT HEALTH CLAMPS UNDER THE SHRINKING MAXIMUM, which is the part worth knowing: an ally kept topped up loses real health on the way down, while one sitting at half never notices it. That is deliberate - it rewards healing them INSIDE the window rather than after it. The loan is temporary in the strictest sense: it is unwound at the end of the battle whatever state it is in, so no lent health ever follows a hero out of the fight.

short: The Berserker keeps HALF the biggest Frenzy bonus he reaches, even after he is healed back up.
long: Blood Frenzy pays the Berserker +2% damage for every 5% of maximum health he is MISSING, so his power rises as he falls - AND +2% for every {=Unit.FRENZY_RAGE_PER_STEP} Rage he has SPENT this battle, which is the half of it he controls. Five Rage is 5% of a full Rage bar, so both terms pay at the same rate off their own bar. The two are ADDED and then capped at twenty steps, one past where the missing-health term tops out while he lives: spending Rage fills the band SOONER, never deeper, so a Berserker already at death's door gains at most one step from it and one who is untouched is no longer stuck at zero. Rage spent counts what actually left the bar, so a card that hands some back is worth only the difference and a waived cost is worth nothing. The floor is the half of it people miss: the highest bonus he reaches in a battle leaves a permanent mark worth HALF of it, and his live bonus never drops below that mark for the rest of the fight. Heal him to full and he keeps the floor. It is why diving early is worth something even if the heroes pull him straight back out, and it resets with each new battle. ONE THING CHANGES IT. UNSLAKED (draft card) makes it keep the FULL bonus for a few turns, so the play is to cast it and then dive. BOIL OVER (draft card) does not touch it: it pours the whole Rage bar out as damage, and that Rage counts as spent like any other.

short: The Warden's Block chance rises with every hit that gets through - and a successful Block throws all of it away.
long: Heavy Plating gives the Warden a flat 15% Block chance, and adds another 8% every time an attack gets THROUGH him, up to +40%. It is bad-luck protection: the longer he goes without blocking, the likelier the next block becomes. THE CATCH IS THAT BLOCKING RESETS THE CLIMB TO ZERO, which is what makes his defence a sawtooth rather than a ramp. THREE DRAFT CARDS ANSWER THE RESET AND TWO OF THEM CANNOT BE USED TOGETHER. ANVIL stops Blocking resetting the climb at all, so it reaches its ceiling and stays there. RECOMPENSE is paid BY the reset instead, returning Rage equal to the percentage points it took. Holding both means the second is paid nothing while the first is up - they are two answers to the same problem rather than a stack. TURN THE BLADE ignores the reset entirely and makes each Block deal Break damage back to the attacker.

short: A second cast that could not improve an effect is refused rather than wasted.
long: Re-applying most statuses takes the BETTER of the two on both counts - the longer duration and the stronger power, never simply the newer one. (Four have a rule of their own, in their own entries: Burn adds its turns, Chill adds a stack and restarts its clock, Poison adds a stack and restarts its clock, and Ruin adds a stack.) That matters because a great many powers are read LIVE at the moment of the cast: Vespers is worth a fifth of the Cleric's own maximum health, Nexus Ward a fifth of the Mage's, Divine Shield better than a third of the Devout's. Casting one of them again while it still stands can therefore produce a SMALLER number than the one already on the board. The smaller number is discarded; the turn, the resource and the cooldown are not. SO THE GAME REFUSES THE CAST INSTEAD. When an ability's whole effect is the status it applies, and everything it could reach already holds that status for at least as long and at least as strongly, the button greys out and its tooltip names what is already standing. There is nothing to learn card by card and no ability that quietly departs from it. THE LIMIT IS DELIBERATE AND WORTH KNOWING: an ability that ALSO strikes, heals or converts a resource still casts even when its buff would not improve, because that half is worth the turn on its own. Funeral Pyre still smothers a fire for Mana, Stabilize still vents Resonance and heals, Battle Shout still pays its Rage. Only the pure buffs, wards, marks and locks are refused. GLACIAL PRISON is one of them: its whole payload is the Chilled and the freeze, so a second one onto an enemy already held writes nothing and is refused - though only once EVERY enemy in front of you is frozen, since any unfrozen one is still a legal target.

short: Two afflictions meeting on one body can join into a stronger one.
long: Some afflictions JOIN when they meet: the second lands on a body already carrying the first, and the two become ONE stronger status, with one chip. A status made of two is SECOND-DEGREE; one made of three would be THIRD-DEGREE, and each degree is stronger than the last. What it is made of still stands: every card that asks whether the body carries one of its ingredients finds it, and anything that counts how many DIFFERENT afflictions a body carries counts each ingredient - so joining never costs breadth. NOTHING RUNS TWICE: the ingredients' effects are not repeated, they are carried. It lasts only as long as the SHORTER of its ingredients would have, so the window to build on it closes with it; when that one runs out, the other stands alone again with what it had left. A cleanse takes it whole, as one status - all but an enemy mender's Cleansing Rite, which thaws a chill inside one a stack at a time, as it thaws any chill. Casting an ingredient again follows that ingredient's own rule. ONE IS KNOWN SO FAR: Rupture, Burn and Chilled.
